Summary
Data source overview: “To Trust Or Not To Trust a Classifier” introduces the Trust Score framework, a density-based post-hoc method for deciding when a classifier’s prediction should be trusted. The paper provides (1) theoretical guarantees that distance-ratio trust scores correlate with Bayes-optimal correctness even in high-dimension by exploiting intrinsic manifold structure, and (2) extensive experiments on UCI, MNIST, SVHN and CIFAR that show the trust score outperforms model confidence in identifying both trustworthy and suspicious examples.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[87]  
Inference strategy justification: The text explicitly states the risk of costly errors caused by untrustworthy predictions, describes deficiencies of model confidence calibration, develops theoretical insights into density level-sets, lays out Algorithms 1 & 2, and validates them empirically. Interventions are inferred directly from the authors’ suggested applications (reject option, monitoring, parameter tuning) and mapped to deployment phases with weak-to-medium evidence ratings.  
Extraction completeness explanation: All causal-interventional pathways from risks through methods, findings and into actionable interventions are captured; framework components are decomposed; no isolated nodes remain.  
Key limitations: The paper is narrow in scope (classifier trust), so downstream safety interventions are limited to rejection/monitoring rather than core training changes. Some edges rely on moderate inference (confidence 2) where authors imply but do not test deployment monitoring.

Improvements to instruction set
1. Provide a concise glossary of approved edge verbs with definitions to minimise synonym ambiguity during massive-scale merging.  
2. Allow citing paragraph numbers instead of long section titles in node/edge rationales for papers lacking clear headings.  
3. Clarify whether multiple risk nodes feeding the same downstream path require separate full paths or can be merged at the problem analysis layer to reduce duplication.  

These tweaks would streamline the extraction process and enhance consistency across the 500 k-source corpus.
